'''Robert Calderbank''' (born 28 December 1954) is a professor of [[computer science]], [[electrical engineering]], and [[mathematics]] and director of the Information Initiative at [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://today.duke.edu/2013/03/calderbankiid |title=Calderbank to Direct Interdisciplinary 'Big Data' Effort at Duke|date=8 March 2013 }}</ref>   He received a [[BSc]] from [[University of Warwick|Warwick University]] in 1975, an [[MSc]] from [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] in 1976, and a PhD from [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] in 1980, all in mathematics. He joined [[Bell Labs]] in 1980, and retired from [[AT&T Labs]] in 2003 as Vice President for Research and [[Internet]] and [[computer network|network]] systems. He then went to [[Princeton University|Princeton]] as a professor of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and [[Applied mathematics|Applied and Computational Mathematics]], before moving to Duke in 2010 to become Dean of Natural Sciences.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://today.duke.edu/2010/05/calderbank.html |title=Duke Names Princeton Professor Dean of Natural Sciences|date=June 2010 }}</ref>

His contributions to [[coding theory|coding]] and [[information theory]] won the [[IEEE Information Theory Society]] Paper Award in 1995 and 1999.<ref>{{cite web|title=Information Theory Society Paper Award|publisher=[[IEEE Information Theory Society]]|url=http://www.itsoc.org/honors/information-theory-paper-award|accessdate=2013-03-06}}</ref>

He was elected as a member into the US [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2005 for leadership in communications research, from advances in algebraic coding theory to signal processing for wire-line and wireless modems.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nae.edu/MembersSection/Directory20412/30339.aspx |title=NAE Members Directory - Dr. A. Robert Calderbank |publisher=[[United States National Academy of Engineering]] |accessdate=2013-03-06}}</ref> He also became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>

Calderbank won the 2013 [[IEEE Richard W. Hamming Medal]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pratt.duke.edu/news/calderbank-awarded-ieee-hamming-medal |title=Calderbank Awarded IEEE Hamming Medal |date=5 December 2012 |publisher=[[Duke University]] |accessdate=2013-03-06}}</ref> and the 2015 [[Claude E. Shannon Award]].

He was named a [[SIAM Fellow]] in the 2021 class of fellows, "for deep contributions to information theory".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-announces-class-of-2021-fellows|title=SIAM Announces Class of 2021 Fellows|date=March 31, 2021|access-date=2021-04-03}}</ref>

He is married to [[Ingrid Daubechies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.math.princeton.edu/~ingrid/personalbio.html |title=Ingrid Daubechies' Personal Biography |publisher=[[Princeton University]] |accessdate=2014-10-13}}</ref>
